subject: lean meat
title: What If You Ate Only Protein? You'd Starve With a Full Stomach

scenes.text: What if you ate nothing but lean meat? You'd starve, with a full stomach.
To burn protein, your liver must strip off its nitrogen as urea. That has a ceiling: about 250 to 300 grams of protein a day.
Past roughly 35 percent of your calories from protein, you hit it. Within days: diarrhea, headaches, exhaustion, and a hunger no meal can satisfy.
Arctic hunters called it rabbit starvation. Wild rabbit is almost pure protein. Eat only rabbit and you feel starved in a week, and die in weeks.
The cure was never more food. It was fat. Add fat to the same lean meat and the poisoning stops.
So a plate piled with lean steak can starve you. Your body doesn't run on protein. It runs on what comes with it.

description:
What if you ate only protein? Your liver can only process about 250 to 300 grams of protein a day, because every gram must be stripped of nitrogen and turned into urea. Beyond roughly 35 percent of calories from protein, the body cannot keep up.
Arctic explorers who lived on very lean meat such as rabbit developed protein poisoning, known as rabbit starvation: diarrhea, headache, fatigue and a hunger that food could not satisfy, with death reported within weeks. Adding fat to the same meat prevented it.

first_comment: Polar explorer Vilhjalmur Stefansson lived on meat for a year under doctors' watch, but he kept the fat. Which single food do you think you could survive on?
